Artificer
är-tĭf'ĭ-sēr
n. (a skilled workman; a craftsman in metal, stone, or timber)
Latin artifex, from ars, art, and facere, to make. The Authorized Version uses it for the master craftsman as distinct from the common labourer.

Biblical Definition

The first artificer named in Scripture stands in the line of Cain: “Zillah, she also bare Tubalcain, an instructer of every artificer in brass and iron” (Gen 4:22). Metalworking, music, and the building of cities all appear in Cain's line before the flood, and the Bible reports this without embarrassment. Common grace is real: the arts were given to men, and men under judgment still received them. Isaiah then lists “the cunning artificer” among the pillars of Judah's civil order which the LORD would take away in the day of judgment — the mighty man, the man of war, the judge, the prophet, the prudent, the ancient, the captain of fifty, the honourable man, the counsellor, the cunning artificer, and the eloquent orator (Isa 3:2-3). To remove the skilled craftsmen from a nation is a judgment, because a society that cannot make anything cannot long defend or feed itself. And the highest use of the word's idea is at the tabernacle, where the LORD names Bezaleel and says, I have filled him with the spirit of God, in wisdom, and in understanding, and in knowledge, and in all manner of workmanship. The first man in Scripture said to be filled with the Spirit of God is a craftsman.

Webster 1828 Definition

Webster (1828) defines an artificer as an artist; a mechanic or manufacturer; one whose occupation requires skill or knowledge of a particular kind; also a contriver, an inventor.

expand to see more

ARTIFICER, n. An artist; a mechanic or manufacturer; one whose occupation requires skill or knowledge of a particular kind; as a silversmith or a carpenter.

2. One who makes or contrives; an inventor.

3. In the army, a soldier employed in the mechanical trades.

Key Scripture

Gen 4:22 — "And Zillah, she also bare Tubalcain, an instructer of every artificer in brass and iron: and the sister of Tubalcain was Naamah."

Isa 3:3 — "The captain of fifty, and the honourable man, and the counsellor, and the cunning artificer, and the eloquent orator."

Exo 31:3 — "And I have filled him with the spirit of God, in wisdom, and in understanding, and in knowledge, and in all manner of workmanship,"

Modern Corruption

Manual and technical skill has been quietly demoted beneath academic and professional work, a ranking Scripture nowhere makes and Exodus 31 flatly contradicts.

expand to see more

Exodus 31:1-5 is the passage that ought to have settled this permanently. The first man in the Bible of whom it is said that God filled him with His Spirit is not a prophet, a priest, or a king: it is Bezaleel the son of Uri, and the filling is specified as wisdom, understanding, knowledge, and all manner of workmanship — in cutting of stones, to set them, and in carving of timber. Aholiab is given with him, and the Spirit's gift includes the ability to teach the trade to others (Exo 35:34). Our culture has arranged work in a hierarchy that Scripture does not recognise, in which the man who designs is above the man who builds and the man who advises is above them both, and it has arranged education to match, so that a generation was told that the trades were what happened to those who could not do better. The Reformers took the opposite view and taught it as doctrine: the milkmaid and the magistrate hold callings equally from God, and the question is faithfulness, not station. Paul made tents. The Lord Jesus was known in Nazareth as the carpenter. The line of Cain shows that skill without godliness produces Lamech and his sword-song; Exodus 31 shows that skill filled with the Spirit builds the house of God.

Greek & Hebrew Roots

Hebrew charash (H2796), a craftsman, engraver, artificer in wood, stone, or metal; chakam-leb, wise-hearted, the tabernacle workers; chokmah (H2451), wisdom, which in Exodus includes manual skill.

expand to see more

Hebrew charash (H2796) — a craftsman or artificer; the same noun covers the smith, the mason, and the carver; Genesis 4:22, Isaiah 3:3, 1 Chronicles 29:5.

Hebrew chakam-leb — wise-hearted; the standing description of the tabernacle workmen, where wisdom is a skill of the hands; Exodus 28:3, 35:10.

Hebrew chokmah (H2451) — wisdom; used in Exodus 31:3 of craftsmanship, and in Proverbs of the fear of the LORD, one word for both; Exodus 31:3, Proverbs 9:10.

Usage

"“An instructer of every artificer in brass and iron” — the trades begin in the line of Cain, under common grace."

"“The cunning artificer, and the eloquent orator” — removing the craftsmen is named as judgment on a nation."

"“Filled him with the spirit of God…in all manner of workmanship” — the first Spirit-filled man in Scripture is a craftsman."
